source_interpretation.topic: A common gel method with unresolved per-size schedules
source_interpretation.text: The authors use a PEG-gel precursor and air calcination to obtain a series of lithium-ferrite crystal sizes. The main describes only an overall temperature/time window, so the seven measured size outcomes do not establish seven fully specified synthesis settings. Solvent identity, proportions and detailed thermal history remain open fields.

source_interpretation.topic: Thermal analysis is evidence about the precursor
source_interpretation.text: The source assigns thermal events to nitrate/PEG decomposition and ferrite formation. This DTA experiment is heated in oxygen at 10 °C/min; its atmosphere and ramp must not be copied into the separately reported air-calcination recipe. The plotted formation event at 303 °C is an analytical assignment, not a universal synthesis setpoint.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1, DTA method and Figure 1

source_interpretation.topic: Size-dependent magnetism and a source-proposed surface explanation
source_interpretation.text: The authors observe lower saturation magnetization for smaller crystals and suggest a surface effect, citing reference 5. That proposed explanation is retained as interpretation; this paper does not directly resolve surface chemistry or spin configurations. Its normalized magnetization curves and coercivity trends are kept as plots, without invented numerical sample values.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Magnetic discussion, Figures 3–4 and reference 5

source_interpretation.topic: Curie temperature has a different reported size dependence
source_interpretation.text: Table I reports 580 °C for the 9.1 nm sample and 620 °C for the 16.4, 22.6, 32.4 and 46.7 nm samples. The bulk 620 °C row is attributed to reference 6. The table does not report values for the 27.3 nm or greater-than-100 nm outcomes, and those values are not filled by interpolation.

source_interpretation.topic: Limits of structural and magnetic labels
source_interpretation.text: The paper reports spinel-type LiFe5O8 and agreement between XRD- and TEM-based average crystal sizes. It supplies no TEM image, shape distribution or atom coordinates. Unresolved trace/symbol assignments and the anomalous printed conversion in Figure 4 remain visible, rather than being silently corrected.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, XRD/TEM methods, Figures 2–4 and captions
